svg.text: Cloud-native raster ecosystem — by architectural layer
where each tool lives · which resampling families it covers · read-time vs. post-load · native-grid I/O vs. integrated warp

g.text: Separable from loading. Same layer, multiple input→output variants. Community is consolidating here for correctness-critical work.
the Points → Grid track, different math families.
(zonal statistics — raster values aggregated onto polygon geometries)
Same family as 4a F3/F4, different output shape (polygon zones, not a grid).
xagg and exactextract support area-weighted mode (F3); rasterstats does stat-agg (F4).
zagg's polygon-zone output (Phase 2) lands here — same math family as 4c,
same output shape, different input substrate (sparse observations vs. raster).
F1 kernel convolution at sparse query points — same math as 4a reprojection,
different target structure. Common in ML pipelines and tile-server APIs.
Layer 3 — Loader + read-time warp (STAC → lazy xarray)
Fetches pixels & warps inside each dask chunk. Fast (overview-aware) but commits to a target grid at open time. Family 1 only.
WarpedVRT per chunk · GDAL full set
stackstac / odc-stac inherit GDAL's full kernel menu.
lazycogs trades that for async + no-GDAL operational simplicity.
Read-time warp is only sound when the target grid is known early
and the operation is local — i.e., only Family 1.
Layer 2 — Cloud I/O (native grid, no resampling)
Returns pixels in their native CRS/grid. Defers all resampling to the consumer. Native-grid loaders shown here; underlying filesystem, readers, codecs, and backends are detailed separately.
pre-built Parquet metadata index · byte-range reads
VirtualiZarr manifest · zero-copy Zarr view over TIFFs
loaders + any Layer-4 sublayer = the separable pattern;
the consumer picks the family that matches the data's semantics.
Formats: COG · GeoTIFF · NetCDF · HDF5 · HDF4 · Zarr v2/v3 · GeoZarr · GRIB2. Virtualization: Kerchunk · VirtualiZarr · GDAL VRT · GDAL GTI · DMR++ · Icechunk.
Object storage: S3 · GCS · Azure · HTTPS · local. Access via fsspec / obstore / GDAL VFS / Icechunk. Readers (sync + async) and codecs sit above.
Loader-integrated warp (Layer 3) saves I/O via overview selection but bakes the target grid into the loader API and is limited to Family 1.
Separable pattern (Layer 2 → any Layer 4 sublayer) composes any family with any loader but can't do overview-aware reads.
Direction: loaders should expose a "native-grid" mode. Grid-math tools across Layer 4 should share a grid protocol so indexing, sharding,
and cell-assignment are reusable primitives. OpenEO's reference implementation has already picked the separable side.
